topic: Orange, the earless cat (@earlesspotato), is offered a pale-yellow ice cream bar and leans in for a cautious sniff and lick before it is taken away.
summary: A ginger cat whose ears were surgically removed after an ear tumour studies an ice cream bar held in front of his face, gives it one careful lick, then watches it disappear with a completely deadpan expression. The missing ears give him a perfectly round, potato-like head, which is why the internet calls him 'earless hachimi'.

research.audience: Cat lovers and casual pet-video viewers worldwide; English-speaking US/UK/PH/IN traffic is the bulk of Shorts pet distribution, plus a large existing curiosity audience already searching for this specific cat after he went viral on Douyin, TikTok and Instagram.
research.hook: 0.75s in, the ice cream rises into frame right under the cat's chin — the viewer immediately asks 'is he going to eat that?' The second hook is the head itself: no ears, perfectly round, which reads instantly on a small screen.
research.competition: Most uploads of this cat are raw reposts with burned-in captions, loud meme audio and no context. They explain nothing about why he has no ears, so the top comment on nearly every one is 'what happened to his ears?'
research.gap: Answer the ear question in the first line of the description, and add the thing every cat owner actually wants to know — whether a cat should be licking ice cream at all. That turns a silent repost into something with a reason to exist.

titles: The Cat With No Ears Tries Ice Cream
youtube.title: The Cat With No Ears Tries Ice Cream
youtube.description:
Orange is a ginger cat with no ears. They were removed completely after an ear tumour, and despite how he looks he can still hear perfectly fine — the surgery left him with a round, potato-shaped head, which is why people online call him the earless hachimi.

Here he gets an ice cream bar held right under his chin. One careful sniff, one lick, and then the most unbothered stare you will see today.

Worth saying, since it comes up every time: most adult cats are lactose intolerant, so ice cream is not a treat to give them. A single lick of plain ice cream is unlikely to hurt a healthy cat, but dairy, sugar and fat all sit badly with an obligate carnivore, and anything with chocolate or a sugar-free sweetener is genuinely dangerous. A chilled spoonful of their own wet food does the same job safely.
